input.summary:
parts/room-20.mjs (west hall bath) now passes make.sh with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE line, but the part places 0 blocks: all 25 furniture writes were refused.
The refusals are not fixable inside this module. The mansion shell carves the whole room interior as air, and runParts locks those cells (air included), so no cell in the bath is writable.
I removed the furniture writes (pre-fix copy at /tmp/room-20.before-lock-fix.mjs). make.sh writes build.nbt.
left: The west hall bath is empty. Its furniture (tub, basin, barrels, chest, stool, towel post, candles, lanterns, chains) is in /tmp/room-20.before-lock-fix.mjs and needs re-adding once rooms can take fit-out.

Root cause is in shell.mjs (interior box fill and carve to air at y3..17) combined with runParts' write lock (build.mjs ~line 220). Fix: leave room interiors unowned air, or let non-carving room parts write into shell-carved air, then re-run this part.
The other room parts (entrance hall through bedroom 7 and the rest) report 0 placed with no refusals, so they are probably stubs, or they will hit the same lock once they write.

waste.what: Worked out by hand which earlier part owned the refused cells. The REFUSED line shows only 8 of 25 cells, and the owner (the shell's interior air carve) had to be traced by reading shell.mjs and build.mjs.
waste.cost: about 6 tool calls: reading parts-report.json, shell.mjs and the runParts lock logic
waste.tool: runParts' REFUSED message should name the owning part and whether the owned cell is air, e.g. 'owned by mansion shell (air carve)', and report the full count, not the first 8.

waste.what: Checked each block id against palette.json by hand, one node snippet plus an mcd blocks --check.
waste.tool: The runParts palette report only counts blocks that landed, so refused writes never get a palette check. A preflight that reports off-palette ids for refused writes too would catch them in one pass.

waste.what: Deleted the furniture layers by hand because the lock makes them unplaceable. A tool could say up front which cells of a part are locked and which are writable.
waste.cost: one file rewrite, plus a backup copy
waste.tool: A dry-run or 'mcd plan' style command that prints the writable cells of each room for a given part list, so a designer sees the lock before writing layers().

companions.task: Fit the bath's tub (water_cauldron on cauldron ends) and basin wash stand once the room interior accepts fit-out, checking the tub's water level and the drain side.
Build the dresser barrels, the chair by the basin, and the towel post into the walls, with the lane x41..42 kept clear from the door to the tub.
Hang and check the lantern and chain light so every floor cell reads 8+ in mcd light.
